pr.title: Plan launching Claude Code and Codex sessions from the console
pr.head: 831a27edae19c7b2b471730f8b22d682b7387065

summary: Projector’s planned terminal console lets you answer and discuss work across live agent sessions. This draft extends it with a form that starts a Claude Code or Codex session in a chosen checkout, so each session does not need its own terminal window.

The console launches each host through its command-line interface, tracks startup in a local record, and opens a session’s chat on demand. This pull request adds only the plan; it implements no launcher.

The plan remains draft with priority next. Approval prompts, matching Claude Code background IDs, attaching Codex to a daemon-held thread, and prompts that match Claude Code subcommands remain explicit open questions. They do not assert implementation readiness.

cards.title: Review result
cards.html: The earlier prompt-option finding is fixed: both launch commands end options with -- before the prompt, and acceptance cases cover a leading-hyphen prompt. Read-only parser checks, the required gate, exact-head CI, and project metadata checks pass.

groups.title: Start sessions and open their chats
groups.kicker: A draft design for launching from the console home list
intro: The New session form selects a host and checkout, accepts a name and prompt, and starts the host without a shell. A launch record lets the console show starting or failed before the session joins the live list.

The Chat key attaches through claude attach or codex resume. Inside tmux it opens a pane; elsewhere it temporarily hands the console’s terminal to the host. Fake executable tests check arguments and startup behavior, while real host approval and attachment behavior stays unresolved.

files.note: Adds the launch form, delimited command arguments, startup record, chat attachment, acceptance cases, and unresolved host questions.

checks.text: Section 2.1 now ends host options before the prompt. Safe CLI parser checks confirm that Codex treats --help, -v hi, and help as operands after --; Claude Code’s parser also accepts --help as an operand.

Section 6 explicitly leaves Claude Code prompts that match a subcommand unresolved, alongside approval and attachment behavior. This is a draft plan, so these questions do not claim implementation readiness.

Section 7 records a prior real Codex launch and wake test. This review checks the plan against the delivery adapter and uses read-only CLI parsing probes; it does not repeat the historical background-session test.
